item.title: Red bench unveiled at Italian ambassador's residence for femicide victims
item.description: A red bench was installed in the garden of the Italian Ambassador's Villa Bel Air residence in Ta' Xbiex to commemorate women killed by gender-based violence, marked on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Italian Ambassador Valentina Setta said the bench asks people to pause and remember women whose lives were taken, while Equality Minister Rosianne Cutajar also took part in the unveiling ceremony.

Sources: Times of Malta, Malta Independent

item.title: Hotels and restaurants association warns rising costs hurt tourism competitiveness
item.description: The Malta Hotels and Restaurants Association has asked the government to review costs imposed on the tourism sector, objecting to further increases in annual licence fees for five-, four- and three-star hotels and lower-rated establishments without prior consultation. The association says the cumulative burden of higher licence fees, the Budget's increased eco-contribution and costs of employing third-country nationals is becoming hard for operators to absorb, and warned that expanding bed capacity without effective management could trigger a damaging price war.

item.title: Birkirkara council says civic centre has no space for a police station
item.description: Birkirkara local council has called it absurd that responsibility for the lack of a police station plan falls on the council. Interior Minister Glenn Bedingfield said a station cannot be provided in the civic centre because of council objections, while the council said every space is already taken by primary healthcare, the podiatry clinic, POYC, Servizz.gov, the health directorate, active ageing services and the regional library. The station was first outlined in plans about 30 years ago and never proceeded.

item.title: Malta-flagged tanker sinks off Ibiza; one crew member dead
item.description: The chemical products tanker Med Emre, flagged under Malta, sank early on Thursday about 25 nautical miles north of Ibiza while sailing from Algeciras to Barcelona. Seventeen crew were rescued, but one was later confirmed dead in hospital and six suffered minor injuries, notably hypothermia. The vessel was carrying around 66,000 barrels of refined products, and Spanish authorities raced to contain any pollution, with the cause of the sinking still unclear.

item.title: Second woman charged over apartment and car rental scams involving €87,000
item.description: Aline Martinelli Souza, a 38-year-old Brazilian national living in Sliema, was denied bail after pleading not guilty to 11 charges including fraud, forgery and money laundering over alleged rental scams. Her associate Jessika Ravara Zaneli Diniz, 35, of San Lawrenz, Gozo, was remanded on Sunday over similar charges involving some €87,000. Police began investigating on 19 November after a man reported that payments intended for third parties were not going through, in a scheme that also involved car rental start-up costs.

item.title: Transport Malta workers face pay cuts; union threatens to halt fines and clamping
item.description: At least 100 Transport Malta employees had overtime pay deducted this month after failing to clock in or out, with one worker reporting a cut of €1,600. The UĦM – Voice of the Workers registered an industrial dispute and gave the authority until noon on Monday 30 November to pay the amounts due. If the money is not paid, the union said enforcement officers will stop issuing traffic citations and clamping vehicles from 1 December, and that action could widen to other job grades.

item.title: Dalli says COP31 outcome was 'very disappointing' and hits out at oil industry lobbying
item.description: Environment, Energy and Regeneration Minister Miriam Dalli told parliament that the UN climate conference ended without a major agreement and that oil industry lobbying was among the obstacles. Citing the World Meteorological Organisation, she said the world has entered an era of climatic extremes with the Mediterranean a hotspot, and argued Malta is already seeing drought, water scarcity and longer heatwaves. She said climate spending accounts for 4% of total government expenditure, with 56% of the climate allocation going to adaptation and resilience, and defended electricity subsidies as necessary to keep energy prices affordable.

item.title: Audit report: 32 local councils given qualified opinions; 13 had negative working capital
item.description: The Auditor General's annual report on local government, presented to Speaker Carmelo Abela, found 32 of 53 councils received qualified audit opinions for 2025 for lack of supporting documentation, five were flagged over going-concern uncertainty, 13 recorded negative working capital and 18 a deficit. Mosta's negative working capital was the largest at €1,014,200, followed by Ħ'Attard (€706,966) and Qormi (€294,490).

item.title: Government to open call for Grand Harbour regeneration proposals
item.description: Energy Minister Miriam Dalli said the government is preparing a call for proposals to redevelop parts of Grand Harbour, following public consultation and expressions of interest from local and international investors. International consultants are assessing whether the redevelopment options are financially viable. She listed 2027 budget allocations of €400 million for energy subsidies, €212 million for energy infrastructure, €438 million for climate action and €63 million for greening projects, and said preparatory cleaning work has begun at Manoel Island.

item.title: PN questions €1.6 million allocation for animal aftercare clinic
item.description: Nationalist MPs argued during the Energy and Environment budget debate that funding for an animal aftercare clinic has been raised from €600,000 to €1.6 million while questions about the facility remain unanswered. MP Janice Abela Chetcuti said dozens of parliamentary questions on the matter have been deferred, while MP Andrew Agius asked whether the national animal hospital will run through a private concession and called for a public veterinary service in Gozo. Parliamentary Secretary Alicia Bugeja Said replied that the directorate's management structure is being strengthened.

item.title: ERA orders fish processing plant at Ħal Far to stop operating
item.description: The Environment and Resources Authority issued a suspension and compliance order on the fish by-products plant at Ħal Far after odour complaints were confirmed again in October, a problem reported since 2022. The plant must halt operations until an independent engineer verifies that its odour-reducing machinery is adequate and operating correctly. The Birżebbuġa local council has petitioned for the matter to be scrutinised in parliament.

item.title: 827 people registered as organ donors in first ten months of 2026
item.description: Health Minister Ian Borg told parliament that 827 people registered as organ donors between January and October 2026, compared with 587 for the whole of 2025, with 30,900 people on the donor register by end of October. Of the 2026 registrations, 538 were women, 288 men and one person was recorded under another gender category. The 2024 total was 1,373.

item.title: 31 people stopped receiving the Carer's Grant since 2021
item.description: Figures given to parliament by Social Policy and Family Minister Michael Falzon show 31 people stopped receiving the Carer's Grant since its introduction in January 2021, with 201 applications recorded up to September 2026. Stated reasons include the death of the beneficiary, payment moving from one parent to another, a child with severe disability entering an institution, or a review by the Professional Board lowering the disability level below the 75% threshold. Eligibility was extended in 2025 to parents of severely disabled children under 16.

item.title: Activists hold symbolic procession for female victims of violence
item.description: Moviment Graffitti organised a procession of mourning, remembrance and resistance in Republic Street, Valletta, to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. The event, titled "I am Jane Doe", focused on non-fatal violence against women whose cases go unreported. Participants wore white blood-stained dresses and carried candles, and speakers called for accessible, timely protection and specialised support services.

item.title: Christmas lights switched on in Valletta by 10-year-old transplant patient
item.description: Ellie Portelli, who had a successful liver transplant as a toddler, switched on the festive lights on Republic Street, with Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea and Valletta Cultural Agency chairman Jason Micallef present. A Christmas tree near Parliament and the Nativity crib in St John's Square were also lit. The Valletta Cultural Agency is running a month of festivities, "Christmas in the Capital", ending with New Year's Eve in St George's Square.

item.title: PN asks who will be responsible for the new Malta in Motion agency
item.description: Shadow sustainable mobility minister Ivan Castillo said it is unclear who will be accountable for decisions once the proposed Malta in Motion agency is set up alongside Transport Malta and Infrastructure Malta. He noted the official plan gives rapid transit planning five years and construction a further ten, so the project could take 15 years to complete, and that the government has not presented an equivalent fallback if it is delayed or underfunded.

item.title: 27-year-old released on electronic monitoring over 56 sexual exploitation charges
item.description: Gian-Luke Gambin, who pleaded not guilty, was granted bail under an electronic monitoring order after being arrested in June on 56 charges involving alleged sexual exploitation and child grooming through fake social media profiles. Police identified at least nine alleged victims, seven of them minors, with the youngest aged 10. The case was triggered by an incident involving two sisters aged 10 and 12 and reports from other teenagers who contacted police.

item.title: Over 90% of Gozitans say they have faith in the Church and priests
item.description: A new Diocese of Gozo survey of 439 residents found 70.6% of respondents attend Sunday Mass, with 70% expecting religious life on the island to decline over the next decade. Attendance shows a clear generational gap: 83% of those over 55 attend Mass weekly, compared with 54.5% of those under 35 and 60.3% in the 35–54 age group. The survey was conducted by telephone between late June and mid-August 2026.

item.title: Eight-storey hotel proposed on Ta' Xbiex office block
item.description: FES Projects Ltd is seeking planning permission to partly demolish and convert the NFS LifeStar Building on Testaferrata Street, adding four floors to create an eight-storey, four-star hotel with 83 rooms. The proposal, PA/08066/26, includes a ground-floor reception and bar, a restaurant and a recessed top-floor pool, with two basement levels for a gym, indoor pool and car park. The Environmental Health Directorate and Enemalta have raised issues over the swimming pools and wastewater discharge.

item.title: GWU wants recruitment agencies to absorb added costs for non-European workers
item.description: The General Workers' Union is asking recruitment agencies to absorb part or all of the added expenses the government will introduce for non-Europeans in 2027, and has urged non-European workers to join a union of their choice to protect their rights. The GWU called the budget resilient with positive measures on social protection and purchasing power, but said further action is needed on vulnerable workers, wages and working conditions.

item.title: St Julian's council to appeal 40-apartment permit at Libyan institute
item.description: St Julian's local council has agreed to appeal the Planning Authority's approval of 40 apartments within the grounds of the Libyan Higher Vocational Institute in Ta' Giorni, together with 51 parking spaces. The council will take the case before the Environment and Planning Review Tribunal and has urged residents to file objections. The development was approved on the grounds that the apartments would be used exclusively as accommodation for students and staff.

item.title: Man jailed 15 years for raping and exploiting three girls
item.description: Abdiladeef Abdirahman Hassan, 30, was sentenced to 15 years and six months after admitting to raping, sexually exploiting and trafficking three girls aged 13 and 14, as well as cannabis trafficking. The offences took place between March 2020 and the preceding years at a residence in San Ġwann and a flat in Birżebbuġa. The case began when a school reported that a 14-year-old was in possession of drugs, and police found the girls had been given cannabis by the accused.

item.title: Isla residents map alleged seafront permit breaches
item.description: Residents' group ATAL has compiled an interactive map of Planning Authority permits for every restaurant and café along the Isla seafront, comparing what operators are authorised to occupy with photographs and videos of what is on the ground. The initiative follows a parliamentary reply in which the Minister for Accommodation and Lands said officials inspect tables and chairs on public land. ATAL cites businesses whose outdoor seating was refused in 2004 and 2007 but which now occupy the quay.

item.title: VAT inspections stopped entirely in election month, minister confirms
item.description: Statistics tabled in parliament by Finance Minister Clyde Caruana show VAT inspections fell from an average of 468 a month in the first quarter to 26 in April and zero in May, the month of the general election, against 628 inspections over the same two months a year earlier. Inspections resumed in June with 350 checks, rising to 759 in September. A total of 3,759 inspections were carried out between January and October, 110 fewer than in the same period of 2025.

item.title: Months of roadworks ahead on key route into the Three Cities
item.description: Roadworks on Triq Għajn Dwieli, which links Paola with the Three Cities, will run into 2027, with the road already partly closed since September. The Water Services Corporation expects its phase of a three-phase water infrastructure project to finish by the end of March 2027, installing a potable water trunk from Qrendi reservoir as an alternative supply for the Three Cities. Paola mayor Jason Silvio said the wider project could take up to a year.

item.title: Cruise tourists to be diverted from Valletta to ease capital overcrowding
item.description: The tourism ministry is working with the Malta Tourism Authority and cruise operators on a plan to give arriving passengers a wider choice of destinations in Malta and Gozo, to reduce the concentration of tourists in Valletta. Tourism Minister Jo Etienne Abela told parliament the aim was to safeguard the sector, which employs one in every five workers. Malta welcomed around four million tourists in 2025 and could exceed its 2035 target of 4.5 million arrivals this year.

item.title: Gozo Tourism Association proposes €4 nightly eco-contribution, warns of 2027 cancellations
item.description: The Gozo Tourism Association has formally submitted its position on the proposed revision of the eco-contribution regime to the Prime Minister and the ministers for Finance, Tourism and Gozo. The association proposes a uniform €4 eco-contribution per person per night across all tourist accommodation in Gozo, capped at seven nights per stay, and asks that the new rates be postponed to 1 July 2027 with all Gozo revenue reinvested on the island. Newsbook reports the association also raised fears of tour cancellations in 2027.

item.title: No VAT inspections took place in May, election month
item.description: Figures tabled in parliament by Finance Minister Clyde Caruana show VAT inspections fell from 653 in March to 26 in April and stopped entirely in May, the month of the general election. The reply, to a question by Nationalist MP Mark Anthony Sammut, gave no reason for the drop. Inspections resumed in June and reached 759 in September, the highest monthly figure in the report.
